reference_analyses.implementation_summary: Fit treatment-only Cox partial likelihood and project each arm through the Breslow baseline. For jackknife uncertainty, assign every participant one of 20 group labels within randomized-arm strata before inspecting outcomes, so that each label is represented approximately equally in each arm. Within each arm, encode each participant identifier as UTF-8, order participants by the raw SHA-256 digest of that encoding, and assign labels 0 through 19 cyclically in that order. For each of the G = 20 refits, delete all participants carrying one label from every arm, then refit the nuisance and target models. Retain the reproducible group assignment with the analysis code. If theta[-g] is the complete-refit estimate after deleting group g, calculate SE = sqrt((G - 1) / G * sum_g((theta[-g] - mean_g(theta[-g]))^2)). Form the two-sided 95% interval around the full-sample estimate using the 0.975 Student-t quantile with G - 1 degrees of freedom.

reference_analyses.implementation_summary: For every continuous baseline covariate, compute Harrell knots at the empirical 0.05, 0.35, 0.65, and 0.95 quantiles in all randomized participants; standardize with the analysis-sample mean and sample standard deviation (ddof=1). With standardized value z and standardized knots k1<k2<k3<k4, use basis z plus h_j(z)=(z-k_j)_+^3-(z-k3)_+^3*(k4-k_j)/(k4-k3)+(z-k4)_+^3*(k3-k_j)/(k4-k3) for j=1,2; do not apply any further basis scaling. Fit the Cox/Breslow model with every basis term, treatment, and every treatment-by-basis interaction; predict both arms for randomized participants meeting the prespecified baseline BMI threshold and average their horizon risks. cells.controlled_condition: Background risk falls by a tenth across the rollout, as in stepped-wedge maternity trials; the declared period model separates the pathway from the secular trend

reference_analyses.implementation_summary: Code period as floor(entry_time / 14 days), code intervention as 1 when entry_time is at or after switch_time. Fit the horizon outcome by inverse-observation-weighted least squares with one indicator for every observed period plus intervention and no separate intercept. The intervention coefficient is the common additive risk difference; extending it to periods without both arms requires the declared common-effect mean model. For jackknife uncertainty, let G be the number of randomized clusters and delete one complete cluster per refit. Refit the period and treatment model after each deletion. If theta[-g] is the complete-refit estimate after deleting group g, calculate SE = sqrt((G - 1) / G * sum_g((theta[-g] - mean_g(theta[-g]))^2)). Form the two-sided 95% interval around the full-sample estimate using the 0.975 Student-t quantile with G - 1 degrees of freedom.
reference_analyses.interpretation: Risk under pathway assignment at delivery minus risk under usual-care assignment at delivery, standardized to the enrolled cohort's observed calendar-entry distribution.
reference_analyses.label: Period- and cluster-adjusted stepped-wedge risk

reference_analyses.implementation_summary: Use every realized row in monitoring_results.parquet through the terminal analysis look and the planned information fractions and efficacy boundaries in monitoring_plan.csv. procedure.resampling_rule: For jackknife uncertainty, assign every participant one of 20 group labels within randomized-arm strata before inspecting outcomes, so that each label is represented approximately equally in each arm. Within each arm, encode each participant identifier as UTF-8, order participants by the raw SHA-256 digest of that encoding, and assign labels 0 through 19 cyclically in that order. For each of the G = 20 refits, delete all participants carrying one label from every arm, then refit the nuisance and target models. Retain the reproducible group assignment with the analysis code. If theta[-g] is the complete-refit estimate after deleting group g, calculate SE = sqrt((G - 1) / G * sum_g((theta[-g] - mean_g(theta[-g]))^2)). Form the two-sided 95% interval around the full-sample estimate using the 0.975 Student-t quantile with G - 1 degrees of freedom.

negative_control.implementation_summary: Estimate the endpoint proportion within each randomized arm, subtract control from active, and form a nominal 95% Newcombe Wilson interval. For arm proportions pA and pC, compute separate 95% Wilson score limits [LA, UA] and [LC, UC]. With d = pA - pC, the difference limits are d - sqrt((pA - LA)^2 + (UC - pC)^2) and d + sqrt((UA - pA)^2 + (pC - LC)^2). Coverage is approximate, not a uniform finite-sample guarantee. Do not reconstruct this interval from the plug-in standard error.

censoring_ignorability.interpretation: Estimates whether measured baseline prognosis predicts observed follow-up.
censoring_ignorability.threshold: simultaneous lower absolute prognostic censoring log-HR: log(1.25) stressed, log(1.75) fragile, log(3.00) broken

dispersion.interpretation: Checks whether the conditional variance of a count endpoint is compatible with the working Poisson mean-variance relation.
dispersion.threshold: report the Pearson chi-square divided by residual degrees of freedom; interpret departure from one with the endpoint mechanism and use robust uncertainty rather than a universal pass/fail cutoff

endpoint_ascertainment.interpretation: Estimates arm- and prognostic-stratum-specific sensitivity and specificity; unsupported validation cells require sensitivity bounds.
endpoint_ascertainment.threshold: validated observed-versus-adjudicated endpoint discordance: 0.025 stressed and 0.10 fragile; any wholly unsupported prognostic stratum is broken

missingness_pattern.interpretation: Describes whether repeated endpoint availability varies across treatment arms and follow-up times in ways relevant to the declared observation process.
missingness_pattern.threshold: report observed and missing counts by randomized arm and scheduled or recorded time; no universal categorical severity cutoff

model_form.interpretation: Tests whether a linear outcome model omits clinically relevant curvature in baseline BMI prognosis or treatment response. Estimator comparisons separately determine whether that departure changes the treatment contrast.
model_form.threshold: largest simultaneous lower 95% confidence bound for the absolute omitted nonlinear BMI prognostic or treatment-response log hazard-ratio contrast from mean BMI to two standard deviations above the mean

model_residuals.interpretation: Checks for gross mean-model or variance misspecification in a repeated continuous endpoint analysis.
model_residuals.threshold: report residual location and spread across fitted values, randomized arms, and follow-up time; no universal categorical severity cutoff

proportional_hazards.interpretation: Measures time variation in the treatment log hazard ratio over prespecified follow-up intervals.
proportional_hazards.threshold: prespecified method-change boundary: the lower 95% confidence bound for the absolute scaled-Schoenfeld rank-slope range is at least log(1.25); report the continuous diagnostic and its uncertainty without converting it to a categorical severity label

secular_trend.interpretation: Estimates calendar-period outcome change after adjustment for current intervention exposure.
secular_trend.threshold: lower 95% absolute treatment-adjusted secular log-hazard range over the released stepped-wedge periods
